# KarelaDB (KARELA DataBase)

> KarelaDB (formerly KDB) is a SQL database for time-series and relational data, made by Amrit Shrestha: one program with an HTTP/JSON API and web console (port 9900) and the PostgreSQL wire protocol (port 8832). It is not kdb+/q. This is its documentation for AI assistants: every topic is a markdown file whose examples ran on kareladb 0.2.0-dev and show their real results.

How to use it: read this index, then fetch only the topics the task needs. The Agent Skills give the essentials in one file each. Sample tables the examples use are in fixtures/.

## Start here

- [KarelaDB skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/skills/kareladb/SKILL.md): connecting, running SQL over HTTP and PostgreSQL, table design, fast queries, server options, cautions
- [KarelaDB geometry skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/skills/kareladb-geometry/SKILL.md): survey, CAD and 3D data in KarelaDB
- [About KarelaDB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/about-kareladb.md): What KarelaDB is, who made it, what you can use it for, how it keeps your data safe, how fast it is and how it is tested.
- [Quick start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/quick-start.md): Get kareladb, make a database, create a table, add rows, query them and open the web console.
- [SQL basics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/sql-basics.md): How KarelaDB reads SQL text: statements, names, text, numbers, TRUE/FALSE/NULL, comments, errors and reserved words.
- [HTTP API overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-overview.md): How to talk to kareladb serve over HTTP - the address, choosing the database, JSON answers, errors, safety rules and limits.
- [CREATE TABLE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/create-table.md): Make a relational or a time-series table, with partitions, sort order, a dedup key, rounded times and computed columns, or make one from a query with CREATE TABLE ... AS.
- [Limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/limits.md): The sizes and counts KarelaDB allows, what happens at each limit, and the features that are not there yet.

## Getting started

- [About KarelaDB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/about-kareladb.md): What KarelaDB is, who made it, what you can use it for, how it keeps your data safe, how fast it is and how it is tested. Covers: Why the name changed, One program, three doors, What you can use KarelaDB for, How your data is kept safe, How fast it is, How it is tested
- [What's new](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/whats-new.md): Everything added to KarelaDB since 2026-09-12, grouped by what it does for you, with the measured number and the topic that explains it. Covers: 2026-10-22: Grafana and Prometheus, with two ready dashboards, 2026-10-22: cold storage: old partitions in S3, MinIO, R2 or B2, still read by every query, 2026-10-18: streamed reads over the Postgres port run three to four times faster; a view's one-day read in half the time, 2026-10-18: a join to a small table runs as a key lookup; a day's grouping in fewer steps, 2026-10-17: sums over a year of windows and of buy/sell views on the column engine, 2026-10-17: year-long reads of joined and lag views fit in memory, 2026-10-16: big answers stream over the Postgres port; long view ranges run in parts, 2026-10-10: a cold scan keeps the disk busy, 2026-10-09: big scans in a full memory budget stop reading the same files again, 2026-10-06: less work around each statement on the PostgreSQL port, 2026-10-02: big sorted copies fit a 3 GB memory limit, 2026-10-02: reads take turns on a small CPU limit, ...
- [Install packages and the Claude skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/install-packages.md): The Windows and Linux install packages, the Docker image, and the skill file that teaches an AI assistant in another project how to use KarelaDB. Covers: Windows, Linux, Where kareladb finds the console, the help and the skill, Docker, The Claude skill, Building the packages yourself
- [Quick start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/quick-start.md): Get kareladb, make a database, create a table, add rows, query them and open the web console. Covers: Get KarelaDB, Your first database, CREATE TABLE, INSERT and SELECT, kareladb shell, Load the sample data, Open the web console (kareladb serve), Next steps
- [SQL basics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/sql-basics.md): How KarelaDB reads SQL text: statements, names, text, numbers, TRUE/FALSE/NULL, comments, errors and reserved words. Covers: Statements and ;, Upper and lower case, Names and "quoted names", Text: 'single quotes', Numbers, TRUE, FALSE and NULL, Comments, Error messages, Reserved words, Clause words, NULL logic
- [SQL command groups: DDL, DML, DCL, TCL, DQL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/sql-command-groups.md): The five groups of SQL statements, every KarelaDB statement in its group, and the role each group needs. Covers: DDL: Data Definition Language, DML: Data Manipulation Language, DCL: Data Control Language, TCL: Transaction Control Language, DQL: Data Query Language, Which group is my statement?
- [Database models: relational, hierarchical, network, NoSQL, object](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/data-models.md): The five classic kinds of database, and how much of each KarelaDB can be - with a picture and a working example for each. Covers: Relational, Hierarchical, Network, Non-relational (NoSQL), Object-oriented

## Databases & folders

- [Databases and the data folder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/databases.md): Where KarelaDB keeps databases, how to name them, and CREATE DATABASE, DROP DATABASE, SHOW DATABASES and USE. Covers: The data folder, Database names and folder paths, CREATE DATABASE, DROP DATABASE, PURGE TRASH, PURGE VERSIONS, TRUNCATE ALL TABLES, SHOW DATABASES, USE, ALTER DATABASE ... SET DIALECT, ALTER DATABASE ... SET WAL_ARCHIVE, ALTER DATABASE ... SET RESULT_CACHE, ...
- [Time travel and branches: SELECT ... AS OF, CREATE DATABASE ... BRANCH OF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/as-of-and-branches.md): Read a table as it was at an earlier time or commit, undo a bad change with one query, and make a full writable copy of a database in a moment, without copying its files. Covers: SELECT ... AS OF, How far back, CREATE DATABASE ... BRANCH OF
- [Queries across databases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/cross-database-queries.md): Read a table of another database on the same server as database.table - in SELECT, JOIN, subqueries and INSERT ... SELECT. Covers: Name a table of another database, What works, Changes stay in your database, Rights, Speed, Locks

AS, Relational tables (RECORDS), TIMESERIES, PARTITION BY, SORT BY, DEDUP KEY, ROUND, Computed columns: AS (expr), Stored generated columns: GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr) STORED, Rows that expire: WITH (ttl_column = ...), ...

Covers: BOOL, BOOLEAN, BYTE, SHORT, INT, INTEGER, LONG, BIGINT, FLOAT, DOUBLE, DECIMAL(s), DATE, TIMESTAMP, SYMBOL, ENUM types (CREATE TYPE), ...

Covers: ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, RENAME COLUMN, ALTER COLUMN, DROP PARTITION, SET TTL, DEDUP ENABLE and DEDUP DISABLE, ADD CONSTRAINT ... Covers: SHOW TABLES, SHOW COLUMNS FROM, SHOW CREATE TABLE, SHOW PARTITIONS FROM, QuestDB's meta functions
- [Rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/rules.md): Name a check, the trading hours or the dedup choice of a table once, and KarelaDB applies it to every row written - saying which rule refused a row and why. Covers: CREATE RULE, ALTER RULE, DROP RULE, See the rules: SHOW RULES
- [The trash - UNDROP TABLE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/trash.md): DROP TABLE keeps the table hidden for some days; UNDROP TABLE brings it back with its rows and indexes. Covers: DROP TABLE and the trash, UNDROP TABLE, SHOW DROPPED TABLES

- [UPDATE and DELETE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/update-delete.md): Change rows with UPDATE, remove rows with DELETE, empty tables with TRUNCATE, get the changed rows back with RETURNING, and fix wrong data safely. Covers: UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, RETURNING, Fix wrong rows safely
- [Loading many rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/loading-data.md): Load thousands or millions of rows: multi-row INSERT, SQL files, CSV files (POST /imp, COPY), the line protocol and the C++ InsertRows API, with speed tips. Covers: Multi-row INSERT, SQL files: kareladb sql <db> -, CSV files, Over HTTP: POST /exec, Line protocol: POST /write, C++ API: InsertRows, Speed tips, Going back to QuestDB or PostgreSQL, Shadow period: compare QuestDB and KarelaDB
- [Line protocol (POST /write)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/line-protocol.md): Load many rows fast with the InfluxDB line format over HTTP - one line per row, answered with 204. Covers: Line format, Times in the wrong unit, Update some columns: upsert=merge, A table that is not there, POST /write, POST /api/v2/write

## Querying

- [SELECT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/select.md): Choose the columns and values that a query gives back, and the table they come from. Covers: SELECT, *, table.*, AS: column names, SELECT without FROM, FROM, DISTINCT
- [WHERE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/where.md): Keep only the rows you want, with comparisons, IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, IS NULL and time ranges. Covers: WHERE, AND, OR, NOT, =, ==, !=, <>, <, <=, >, >=, BETWEEN, NOT BETWEEN, IN (list), NOT IN (list), time IN 'interval', Interval lists, today() and DECLARE, LIKE, NOT LIKE, ILIKE, NOT ILIKE, SIMILAR TO, NOT SIMILAR TO, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, Row comparison: (a, b) < (x, y), ...
- [Operators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/operators.md): Every operator of KarelaDB SQL, which one is done first, and what NULL does to each of them. Covers: Operator precedence, Arithmetic: + - * / %, Integer division: SET int_division, Comparison operators, || : join text, -> and ->> : parts of JSON, :: : change the type, NULL rules
- [Joins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/joins.md): Put rows of two or more tables side by side: JOIN, LEFT / RIGHT / FULL JOIN, USING, CROSS JOIN, and ASOF / LT / SPLICE JOIN for time series. Covers: JOIN, INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, LEFT OUTER JOIN, RIGHT JOIN, RIGHT OUTER JOIN, FULL JOIN, FULL OUTER JOIN, USING, CROSS JOIN, ASOF JOIN, LT JOIN, SPLICE JOIN, Table aliases, Joining a subquery
- [GROUP BY and HAVING](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/group-by.md): Make one row per group (per symbol, per broker, per account) with totals like count, sum and max, and filter the groups with HAVING. Covers: GROUP BY, ROLLUP, CUBE and GROUPING SETS, Big GROUP BY: many groups and memory, Implicit GROUP BY, HAVING, Columns that are not grouped
- [PIVOT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/pivot.md): Turn the values of one column into columns, like a pivot table in Excel: turnover per symbol with one column per day. Covers: PIVOT (...)
- [ORDER BY, LIMIT, OFFSET](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/order-by-limit.md): Sort the result, and give back only the first rows or one page of rows. Covers: ORDER BY, ASC, DESC, COLLATE: dictionary order, NULLS FIRST, NULLS LAST, LIMIT, OFFSET, Paging
- [UNION and subqueries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/union-subqueries.md): Put the rows of two queries together, and use one query inside another. Covers: UNION ALL, (SELECT ...) as a value, IN (SELECT ...), NOT IN (SELECT ...), EXISTS, NOT EXISTS, FROM (SELECT ...) alias, Correlated subqueries
- [EXPLAIN](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/explain.md): See how KarelaDB will read the tables for a query, without running it; with ANALYZE, run it and see what really happened. Covers: EXPLAIN, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON), EXPLAIN INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, EXPLAIN CALL, The plan lines, Zone maps: partitions skipped by column stats, Answers without reading rows

## Time-series

- [SAMPLE BY](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/sample-by.md): Put rows into time buckets (1 minute, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day, 1 week, 1 month) and make candles. Covers: SAMPLE BY, Intervals, FILL, FROM / TO, ALIGN TO CALENDAR, ALIGN TO FIRST OBSERVATION, TIME ZONE, WITH OFFSET, WEEK START
- [LATEST ON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/latest-on.md): Keep only the newest row of each symbol (or of each group of columns). Covers: LATEST ON, WHERE with LATEST ON, LATEST ON with other clauses, Errors
- [Time and time zones](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/time-and-time-zones.md): How KarelaDB stores times (UTC milliseconds), how to write a local time with its offset (like +05:45), the session's time zone (SET TIME ZONE, --timezone), time zone names, and time ranges with IN '...'. Covers: Storage, Time text, A local time: Nepal +05:45, The session's time zone: SET TIME ZONE, Time zone names, Zones with summer time, IN 'interval' for time ranges, Times in results
- [Trading calendars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/calendars.md): Say which days a market trades - its weekdays, how they changed over the years, and its holidays - and ask it in SQL and in timers. Covers: CREATE CALENDAR, ALTER CALENDAR, DROP CALENDAR, The functions, Find missing days, See the calendars: kdb_calendars, Find the eras in your data: suggest_calendar_eras, Timers on trading days, How it is stored
- [Prices adjusted for splits and bonus shares](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/adjusted-prices.md): Read a price table as if every split and bonus share had always been there - a chart without the jump on the ex-date - while the table keeps the traded prices. Covers: The table of corporate actions, How a row is adjusted, Which columns change, Filters, candles and indicators, Errors
- [Partitions, SORT BY and DEDUP KEY](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/partitions-and-dedup.md): How PARTITION BY, SORT BY and DEDUP KEY of a time-series table change where rows go, their order, and what happens to duplicates; DROP PARTITION deletes old data fast. Covers: PARTITION BY, PARTITION BY time, SYMBOL(col), SORT BY, DEDUP KEY, Ragged seconds: a DEDUP KEY on the minute, A plain INSERT that replaces: dedup_insert, Packed partitions: compression, Appending without rewriting: tail files, Small changes without rewriting: delta files, How a load finds duplicates, Loads without the duplicate check: dedup=skip, DEDUP TABLE, ...
- [Cold storage (S3, MinIO, R2, B2)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/cold-storage.md): Move old partitions of a time-series table to S3-compatible object storage (AWS S3, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2) and keep reading them as if they were local. Covers: Define a store, Turn it on for a table, MOVE PARTITION ... TO COLD and FROM COLD, What a query costs, Watch it: cold_partitions(), /api/stats, /metrics, How a move stays safe, Limits
- [Candles cookbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/candles-cookbook.md): Ready market-data queries: candles from minute data and from trades, daily change, top gainers, volume leaders, 52-week high and low, moving averages and filled gaps. Covers: Candles from minute data, Hourly candles on a local clock (Nepal), Daily candles from trade log trades, Weekly candles, Sunday to Thursday, Monthly and yearly candles, Daily change %, Top gainers and losers, Volume and turnover leaders, 52-week high and low, Moving averages and crossovers, Indicators on candles, Candle and indicator tables kept by a timer, ...

## Functions — math

- [Finance and price functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-finance.md): Money math like Excel (interest, loan EMI, NPV, IRR, XIRR, CAGR), price ticks and pivot points for traders. Covers: cagr, compound_interest, fv, pv, pmt, nper, npv, irr, xnpv, xirr, round_tick, floor_tick, ceil_tick, pivot_point, ...
- [Math functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-math.md): Round and cut numbers, take powers, roots and logarithms, divide safely, put values in buckets, and make random numbers. Covers: abs, round, round_half_even, floor, ceil, ceiling, trunc, truncate, sqrt, cbrt, pow, power, exp, ln, log, log10, ...
- [Trigonometry and probability](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-math-more.md): Sine, cosine, tangent and their inverses, hyperbolic functions, and the normal distribution (chance, bell height and inverse). Covers: sin, cos, tan, cot, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh, normal_cdf, normal_pdf, ...

## Functions — text

- [Regular expressions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-regex.md): Find, count, cut out and replace text with patterns like \d+ (one or more digits). Covers: regexp_like, regexp_substr, regexp_count, regexp_replace, Flags, regexp_match, regexp_matches, regexp_split_to_array, regexp_split_to_table, PostgreSQL flags, Regular expression syntax
- [Text functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-text.md): Change case, cut, trim, pad, search and join text. A letter of any language (Nepali, Chinese, ...) counts as one character. Covers: lower, upper, length, char_length, character_length, octet_length, substr, substring, left, right, trim, btrim, ltrim, rtrim, replace, split_part, ...

## Functions — date and time

- [Date and time functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-date-time.md): Take a time apart, find the weekday, quarter and week, cut, add and build times, count days or months between times, fiscal years (also Nepal's), and write a time as text. Covers: now, systimestamp, year, month, day, hour, minute, second, day_of_week, is_trading_day, date_part, extract, quarter, day_of_year, ...

## Functions — conditional and NULL

- [Conditional and NULL functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-conditional.md): Choose a value with CASE, replace NULL with coalesce, and turn a value into NULL with nullif. Covers: CASE WHEN, CASE value WHEN, coalesce, nullif, NULL rules

## Functions — aggregate

- [Aggregate functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-aggregate.md): Make one value from many rows: count, sum, avg, min, max, first, last, median, percentile, vwap, twap, conditional counts and sums, the row of the maximum, and lists of text. Covers: count(*), count(x), count(DISTINCT x), count_distinct, sum, avg, min, max, first, last, first_not_null, last_not_null, median, ...

## Functions — window and series

- [Window and series functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-window.md): Look at a series of rows: previous and next values, running totals, moving windows, time windows and ranks, with OVER (...). Covers: OVER (...), PARTITION BY (window), ORDER BY (window), ROWS n PRECEDING, ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING, ROWS BETWEEN n PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, ROWS BETWEEN ... FOLLOWING, RANGE BETWEEN, lag, lead, cumsum, cumprod, ...

## Functions — technical indicators

- [Momentum indicators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-indicators-momentum.md): MACD, stochastic, stochastic RSI, Williams %R, CCI, rate of change, momentum and TRIX on candles, with the same results as TA-Lib. Covers: macd, macd_signal, macd_hist, stoch_k, stoch_d, stochf_k, stochrsi_k, stochrsi_d, willr, williams_r, cci, roc, rocp, rocr, mom, momentum, trix
- [Technical indicators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-indicators.md): Moving averages (SMA, EMA, WMA, DEMA, TEMA, TRIMA, KAMA, HMA, VWMA), RSI and ATR on candles, per symbol, with the same results as TA-Lib. Covers: sma, ema, wma, dema, tema, trima, kama, hma, vwma, rsi, atr
- [Trend indicators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-indicators-trend.md): Is the price going up, down or sideways, and how strong is the move? ADX and DI, Aroon, parabolic SAR, Ichimoku, SuperTrend, linear regression and Heikin-Ashi candles. Covers: cross_above, cross_below, plus_di, minus_di, dx, adx, adxr, aroon_up, aroon_down, aroon_osc, sar, parabolic_sar, ichimoku_tenkan, ichimoku_kijun, ichimoku_senkou_a, ichimoku_senkou_b, ichimoku_chikou, ...
- [Volatility indicators and bands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-indicators-volatility.md): How much the price moves: true range, ATR in percent, Bollinger bands, Keltner and Donchian channels. Covers: trange, true_range, natr, bb_upper, bb_middle, bb_lower, bb_percent_b, bb_width, kc_upper, kc_lower, kc_middle, dc_upper, dc_middle, dc_lower
- [Volume indicators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-indicators-volume.md): Is money flowing in or out? On-balance volume, the A/D line, Chaikin money flow and oscillator, MFI, force index and ease of movement. Covers: obv, ad, ad_line, cmf, adosc, chaikin_osc, mfi, efi, force_index, eom, ease_of_movement

## Functions — statistics

- [Correlation and regression](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-correlation.md): Do two series move together? corr, covariance, a straight trend line (regr_slope, regr_intercept, regr_r2), and the beta and alpha of a share against the market. Covers: corr, covar_pop, covar_samp, regr_slope, regr_intercept, regr_r2, regr_count, regr_avgx, regr_avgy, regr_sxx, regr_syy, regr_sxy, beta, alpha
- [Returns and risk](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-returns-risk.md): Returns, drawdown, volatility, z-score and the risk numbers of an investment: Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, information ratio, value at risk and expected shortfall. Covers: pct_return, percent_return, returns, log_return, cum_return, drawdown, volatility, zscore, minmax_scale, max_drawdown, sharpe_ratio, sortino_ratio, calmar_ratio, information_ratio, ...
- [Statistics functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/functions-statistics.md): Describe a set of numbers: spread (stddev, variance, mad, iqr, range), shape (skewness, kurtosis), other averages (geomean, harmonic_mean, mode) and exact percentiles. Covers: stddev, stddev_samp, stddev_pop, variance, var_samp, var_pop, skewness, skew, skewness_pop, kurtosis, kurt, kurtosis_pop, geomean, geometric_mean, harmonic_mean, mode, percentile_cont, quantile_cont, ...

- [The procedure language](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/procedure-language.md): Variables, IF, WHILE, FOR, RETURN, RAISE, PRINT and cursors inside a procedure or trigger body. Covers: DECLARE, SET, IF, ELSIF, ELSEIF, ELSE, WHILE, FOR, RETURN, RAISE, PRINT, EXECUTE (dynamic SQL), Cursors in a body: DECLARE CURSOR, OPEN, FETCH INTO, CLOSE, Limits of the procedure language
- [Calling web services from SQL (http_get, http_post)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-functions.md): http_get and http_post call a web address from SQL, a procedure or a timer. Off until an admin lists the hosts they may call. Covers: http_get, http_post, Reading the answer, Turning them on, What a call may do, Who may call
- [Timers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/timers.md): Let the server run a procedure, a function or any SQL by itself at set times, so a table stays up to date. Covers: Schedules, How a run works, In the console, GET /api/timers, POST /api/timers, Run, turn off, delete, Good to know

FOR UPDATE, Transactions in kareladb shell, Transactions over HTTP, One writer per table, ...

## Users & security

- [Users and roles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/users-and-roles.md): Database users with passwords, and the roles read, write, ddl and admin for every database or for one. Covers: CREATE USER, ALTER USER, ALTER USER ... SET statement_timeout, ALTER USER ... SET timezone, DROP USER, SHOW USERS, GRANT, REVOKE, SET ROLE, Roles: what each one may do, Where users are kept
- [Table rights - GRANT ON TABLE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/table-rights.md): Give a user rights on one table (GRANT SELECT ON TABLE prices), on some of its columns (GRANT SELECT (id, name) ON staff) or on some of its rows (CREATE POLICY), or take some rights of the role away (REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLE ledger). Covers: GRANT ... ON TABLE, REVOKE ... ON TABLE, Column rights, Row rights (row-level security), REVOKE role ON DATABASE
- [API tokens](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/api-tokens.md): Named, revocable secrets for apps - each acts as one user, and DROP TOKEN stops it at once. Covers: CREATE TOKEN, DROP TOKEN, SHOW TOKENS, Where tokens and logins are kept
- [Two-factor login (TOTP)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/two-factor-login.md): A database user can log in to the console and POST /api/login with a password and a 6-digit code from an authenticator app. Covers: ALTER USER ... ENABLE TOTP, kareladb user reset-2fa, Password policy, Session tokens, Step-up codes for dangerous actions
- [Keeping kareladb serve safe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/server-security.md): Keep the server on 127.0.0.1, use users or a token, put HTTPS in front, and pick strong passwords. Covers: --bind, --token, Users and logins, HTTPS in front, Password rules, Checklist
- [TLS (https and sslmode=require)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/tls.md): Encrypt both ports with one certificate - https:// for the HTTP API and the console, sslmode=require for PostgreSQL clients. Covers: Turn it on, A self-signed certificate (auto), What changes for clients, Docker
- [Encryption at rest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/encryption.md): CREATE DATABASE x WITH (encryption = on) - every file, log record and backup of it is encrypted; without the master key a copied disk shows nothing. Covers: Turn it on, Keys, Change the master key, Backups and restore, What is encrypted, Speed
- [Protection - timeouts, limits, safe updates, read-only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/protection.md): Stop slow statements (timeout and cancel), limit the memory of one query and the statements of one user, refuse UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE, and make a database read-only. Covers: SET statement_timeout, Cancel a running statement, DELETE /exec/<id>, Memory limits, --max-queries-per-user, --rate-limit-ip and --rate-limit-user, SET safe_updates, ALTER DATABASE ... SET READ ONLY, Stopping the server without cutting requests off
- [Audit log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/audit-log.md): KarelaDB writes security events (logins, users, DDL, backups, refused rights) and, for chosen tables, every changed row with who, when, old and new values. Covers: SHOW AUDIT, ALTER TABLE ... SET AUDIT ON, The hash chain, SHOW AUDIT VERIFY, GET /api/audit, --audit-keep-days, Erase one user's data

## Backup, check, repair, restore

- [Troubleshooting a running server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/troubleshooting.md): What to look at, and what to change, when the server is slow, readers wait, memory or disk grows, the start is slow, a timer or a backup does not run, or data must come back. Covers: The server is slow, Readers wait for a writer, Errors 55P03 and 40001: the table is busy, Memory is high, The disk keeps growing, The start is slow, or says "last shutdown: not clean", A timer does not run, A backup failed, Getting data back
- [Backup, check, repair and restore](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/backup-and-safety.md): How KarelaDB keeps your data safe, how to make and test backups, and how to get the data back after damage or a mistake. Covers: How KarelaDB protects your data, The log is compressed, When the disk is full, When the system is short of memory, BACKUP DATABASE, CHECK TABLE, CHECKPOINT, kareladb backup, kareladb backups, kareladb verify-backup, kareladb restore, Restore while the server runs, ...
- [Backups on a schedule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/backup-schedule.md): kareladb serve makes a verified backup of every database at set times, checks a second copy on another disk, runs your command to copy each backup off the server, and warns when the last good backup is old. Covers: Where the settings come from, Set a daily backup, --backup-schedule, --backup-copy, --backup-command, --backup-warn-hours, Backup status in /api/info
- [Versions and upgrades](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/versions.md): A new KarelaDB opens the data of an older KarelaDB. An older KarelaDB refuses the data of a newer KarelaDB with "needs a newer KarelaDB" and changes nothing. Covers: kareladb version <db>, SHOW VERSION, kareladb upgrade, Going back to an older version, "needs a newer KarelaDB", The features, Two options named late, Changes that need no format change
- [Standby server: a live read-only copy (--standby-of, kareladb promote)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/standby.md): A second KarelaDB server that copies every database of a primary from its log, a moment behind, and serves reads. Covers: Start a standby, Read-only, How far is it?, Promote: the standby becomes the primary, Starting from a backup, GET /api/wal

## HTTP API

- [HTTP API overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-overview.md): How to talk to kareladb serve over HTTP - the address, choosing the database, JSON answers, errors, safety rules and limits. Covers: All routes, Choosing the database, Answers and errors, GET reads, POST changes, Retrying safely: Idempotency-Key, Logins, tokens and cookies in short, Safety rules, CORS, Limits, Clients, GET /, GET /help, GET /help/, ...
- [Run SQL over HTTP (/exec, /exp)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-exec.md): Run SQL with GET or POST /exec and get JSON, or download the rows of a SELECT as CSV with /exp. Covers: GET /exec, POST /exec, GET /exp, POST /exp
- [Databases over HTTP (/api/databases)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-databases.md): List the databases of a server, create a new one, and drop one (its folder moves to _trash). Covers: GET /api/databases, POST /api/databases, DELETE /api/databases/<name>
- [Saved queries as URLs (CREATE ENDPOINT)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-endpoints.md): Save a SELECT with named parameters under a name; programs then call GET /v/<name>?param=value and get JSON, without sending SQL. Covers: CREATE ENDPOINT, Calling an endpoint, DROP ENDPOINT, How it is stored
- [Health, info, check and backup over HTTP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-server-info.md): Check that the server is alive, read the tables, disk use and health of a database, look for damage, make and list backups, watch deferred trigger queues, and read the server's memory, processor and settings. Covers: GET /health, GET /api/info, GET /api/disk, GET /api/trigger-queue, POST /api/check, POST /api/backup, GET /api/backups, POST /api/restore, POST /api/databases/swap, GET /api/stats, GET /metrics, GET /api/slow-queries, ...
- [Key-value store (Redis-like)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/kv.md): GET, SET, INCR, EXPIRE, DEL, KEYS, MGET and the other Redis string commands, hashes, sets, sorted sets, lists (with BLPOP), SORT and WATCH / MULTI / EXEC over HTTP (POST /kv, one command or a pipeline) and as SQL functions (kv_get, kv_set, kv_incr); PUBLISH / SUBSCRIBE and keyspace events. Keys are kept in memory and in the table _kv. Covers: POST /kv, The commands, Publish and subscribe, A memory cap: CONFIG SET maxmemory, Hashes, sets, sorted sets and lists, From SQL: kv_get, kv_set, kv_incr, The table _kv
- [Sessions and cursors over HTTP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-sessions-and-cursors.md): Keep a transaction open over several HTTP requests with a session, and read a big result a part at a time with a cursor. Covers: POST /session, DELETE /session/<id>, POST /cursor, GET /cursor/<id>, DELETE /cursor/<id>
- [CSV import over HTTP (POST /imp)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-import.md): Send a CSV file to kareladb serve and it loads the rows, making the table from the file when it is new - QuestDB's /imp. Covers: POST /imp
- [Pinned queries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/pinned-queries.md): Pin a SELECT so its result is always ready in the result cache - computed when the database opens, never pushed out, computed again after a write. Covers: GET /api/pins, POST /api/pins, DELETE /api/pins
- [Change revisions: GET /api/rev and kdb_rev()](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/revisions.md): A cheap number per table and per symbol that changes when committed rows change, so a chart polls it and reads its candles again only when they changed. Covers: Which column has revisions, GET /api/rev, kdb_rev
- [Change stream and live subscriptions: changes('t'), GET /api/changes, GET /api/subscribe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/change-stream.md): Every committed INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE of a table as an ordered stream you can resume from its LSN, in SQL or over HTTP, and queries that push their changed rows. Covers: changes('t'), GET /api/changes, How long changes are kept, GET /api/subscribe
- [Logins, tokens and roles over HTTP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/http-login.md): How a program or the console proves who it is - the access token, HTTP Basic, POST /api/login - and the 401, 403 and 429 answers. Covers: Ways to send a login, POST /api/login, POST /api/logout, GET /api/me, The access token (--token), POST /api/session, CSRF: the X-KDB-CSRF header, HTTP Basic, Roles: what each route needs, 401, 403 and 429 answers

Covers: pg_stat_activity, pg_cancel_backend and pg_terminate_backend, query_activity, CANCEL QUERY and cancel_query, pg_sleep, Idle and vanished clients, GET /api/sessions and DELETE /api/sessions/<pid>, pg_stat_statements
- [LISTEN and NOTIFY](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/listen-notify.md): Send a message to every client that listens on a channel when a transaction commits - over the PostgreSQL port (LISTEN) or HTTP (GET /listen, server-sent events). - [Settings - SET, SHOW ALL, ALTER SYSTEM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/server-settings.md): One list of the server's settings behind pg_settings, SHOW ALL, SHOW PARAMETERS and GET /api/settings; SET for a session, ALTER SYSTEM and pg_reload_conf() for the server. - [View data page (browse and edit rows)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/console-data-page.md): Look at the rows of a table in the console and change them with forms - add, edit and delete - without writing SQL. Covers: The screen, Which tables can be edited, What it sends, Notes
- [Keep data page (how long tables keep their rows)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/console-keep-data.md): See every table of a database with how long it keeps its rows, and set "keep only the last N months or years": the older days, months or years are dropped, the newest stay. Covers: The screen, Disk space
- [Monitor panel (memory, processor, caches)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/console-monitor.md): What the server is doing right now - memory it holds, processor it uses, what each database keeps in memory, deferred trigger queues, and the statements running this second. Covers: Warnings and databases opening, The server process, Statements running now, Lanes, Slow statements, Timers, Each database, Server activity, What it does not show
- [Settings page (data folder, old log, capacity, program files and users)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/console-settings.md): Where the server keeps its data, how to point it at another folder, and who may log in - all from the console. Covers: Storage, Old log kept per database, Result cache, Backups, Calls from SQL, Capacity and waits, Program files, Users
- [Comments and suggestions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/feedback.md): How people who use a KarelaDB server send comments, suggestions and problem reports, and how its admins read them. Covers: The page in the console, POST /api/feedback, GET /api/feedback, POST /api/feedback/<id>

## Geometry & CAD

- [Survey, CAD and 3D data: points, drawings, blocks, meshes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Amritshr/kareladb-knowledge/main/docs/geometry-and-cad.md): How to keep survey points, 2D drawings (lines, arcs, polylines, blocks, layers) and 3D meshes in KarelaDB, load only the part a canvas can see, and do distance, area and volume maths in SQL - with the rule that the camera stays in the client. Covers: Coordinates and the one rule, Survey points and control, Raw observations, reduced in SQL, Drawings, layers and entities, Blocks and groups, Partial load: only what the canvas can see, The camera stays in the client, Save, open, undo and history, 3D: vertices, faces, volumes, Measurements in SQL, Limits and what would come next

## Performance tips

Covers: Measure: timings and EXPLAIN, EXPLAIN lines to look for, Filter on time and symbol first, Parameters, variables and computed dates, LIMIT, LATEST ON with a time filter, Bulk INSERT: many rows per statement, Many small writes: --sync-commits batch, Memory: --memory, Big GROUP BY over a UNION, Threads: --threads, Result cache: --cache-mb, ...
